subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@acmecorp.com>, Sofia Torres <s.torres@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the goals you shared, and proposed next steps from Redwood. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points / goals
- Tail latency spikes at peak (35% of requests exceed 300ms) are causing UI timeouts for your chat experience.
- Need predictable per-request latency (95th percentile) under load for a 2048 token context window.
- Throughput target: sustained 500 RPS during business hours, with 2x burst capacity for marketing events.
- Data isolation requirement for user PII and audit logs retention for 12 months.

What we discussed (summary)
- Model: you want to run a 7B-quality causal model for chat; preference for a quantized variant to reduce cost but with strict 95p latency <= 120ms target.
- Topology: we recommended a Dedicated GPU pool in us-west1 with autoscaling and an internal fallback to a smaller model if latency SLOs are at risk.
- Optimization levers: request batching, KV/prefix caching for repeated contexts, and kernel selection for long-context inference.

Action items / next steps
1) Redwood: send a short SLO summary and recommended deployment topology (attached). See acme_slo_summary.pdf and deployment_topology.png.
2) Acme: confirm acceptable SLOs and any hard limits (e.g., 95p must be <= 120ms, or 99p <= 200ms).
3) Redwood + Acme SRE: schedule a follow-up POC plan call to validate throughput under your recorded traffic trace (suggest Wed 11/25).
4) Redwood Sales (David): prepare a POC pricing estimate and mutual action plan.

Attachments: acme_slo_summary.pdf (SLO table + recommended config), deployment_topology.png (diagram).

If this looks right, I’ll loop David for pricing and Dev for the POC runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Recap: technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Thanks Marissa — this is an excellent summary and captures the discussion. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) The 95p target is our primary SLA — yes, we want 95p <= 120ms for user-facing chat generation. If 99p is under 200ms that's acceptable as a secondary goal.
2) Our current traffic shape (attached to the calendar invite) peaks at ~600 RPS for short bursts; steady-state is ~350 RPS. We need the system to handle 2x bursts for predictable degradation, not hard failures.
3) For the POC, we can provide a synthetic trace and a sample of anonymized logs for replay.

Questions:
- Can Redwood’s KV/prefix cache be pinned per-customer (we need strict tenant isolation)?
- For fallbacks: can we do model variant fallback without a service interruption (i.e., downgrade to 2.7B quantized inline)?

We’re fine with the follow-up call — Wed 11/25 AM PST works.

—Amit

amit.shah@acmecorp.com

Subject: Re: Recap: technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Amit — great questions. Quick answers and a bit more detail on the recommended setup (see attached PDF for SLO table).

KV/prefix cache and tenant isolation
- Yes: KV/prefix cache can be scoped per-customer and lives in customer-isolated storage when you deploy on Redwood Dedicated or Private. We can enable encryption-at-rest and tie keys to your KMS.

Model variant fallback
- We support automated fallback to a smaller quantized model without a hard service interruption. The runtime supports dynamic model routing: when queue latency or instance health indicates the primary variant cannot meet the 95p target, requests are routed to a compatible quantized variant. You can configure fallback thresholds (e.g., CPU/GPU queue depth, 95p rollout).

SLOs / performance assumptions
- 95th percentile tail latency target: <= 120ms for generation of up to 1024 tokens on the recommended 7B-quantized variant under steady-state 500 RPS.
- Burst headroom: autoscaling to 2x baseline within 60 seconds for GPU pool with pre-warmed instances.
- Throughput: baseline expected 500 RPS sustained; we’ll run a POC to validate real-world shaping.
- Context window: we tested up to 2048 tokens; beyond that you should expect linear increases in per-token latency.

Suggested deployment topology (summary)
- Dedicated GPU pool in us-west1 behind a smart routing layer.
- Autoscale policy: target CPU/GPU utilization 65–75%, with pre-warm for scheduled bursts.
- KV/prefix caching + per-tenant encryption.
- Canary rollout for model versions with automatic fallback rules.

Next steps I’ll take from Redwood:
- Finalize POC runbook with Dev (replay trace + success criteria).
- Share a short SLO matrix (attached).
- Coordinate a 60-minute POC run on Wed 11/25 AM PST — Dev will lead the infra setup.

Let me know if you want us to include a short cost estimate for the POC compute.

Thanks,
Marissa
